newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse trade just off record high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse trade just off record high.

text.p: Germany's blue chip DAX index ended bourse dealings on Wednesday just shy of its all-time high, buoyed by the firmer dollar, strong Bunds and surprising news from the telecommunications sector.
The 30-share DAX closed floor trading up 11.82 points at 2,702.99, two points off a record of 2,704.74 hit on Monday.
The advance was led by utility stocks RWE and Veba AG, which jumped higher after announcing they were close to an alliance in the lucrative telecoms sector.
The MDAX index of some 70 mid-ranking stocks, which was driven higher Tuesday after news of sportswear maker Adidas' World Cup sponsorship deal, reached a new high of 3,003.09 points.
Dealers noted that the dollar's push above the psychologically crucial 1.53-mark level was partly behind the market's upward push, but that volumes were not strong enough to create any new records.

Telecommunications stocks were among the most actively traded after the alliance news, particularly as RWE had been expected to link up with fellow utility Viag AG and British Telecom rather than Veba and its partner Cable & Wireless.
"The reactions are pretty predictable -- people are getting out of Viag, getting into Veba and RWE. Telecoms are always a big story here," said a Frankfurt dealer.
RWE ended bourse trade up 2.95 marks at 60.60 while Veba rose 68 pfennigs to 81.53 points. Viag declined 21 marks to 581 marks.
